chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Humran, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding the sacrifice of the Nāsibī (those who repudiate the Imams), the Jew, and the Christian: Do not eat their sacrifice until you hear them mention the name of Allah. I said: What about the Magus? He said: Yes.
Did you not hear the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Do not eat from that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned'?

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: Nāsibī (one who repudiates or is hostile to the Imams, a specific Shia term)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians halal if they slaughter it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) establishes that for the People of the Book and Zoroastians, mere general declaration is insufficient; one must explicitly hear the invocation of Allah's name during slaughter to validate the meat. This ruling is grounded in the Quranic command in Surah Al-An'am, which Shia scholars interpret as requiring the specific mention of Allah's name to distinguish permissible slaughter from that of the polytheists who mention other names. The inclusion of the Magus highlights the broader application of this criterion to other monotheistic or quasi-monotheistic communities recognized in Shia jurisprudence.
